status_summary: Both recommendations have been acted on. On 2025-02-05 Attorney General Pam Bondi issued a memo on zealous advocacy that calls for discipline or termination of attorneys who decline to advance good-faith arguments for the administration, and Executive Order 14215 (2025-02-18) says the President's and Attorney General's legal interpretations bind executive branch employees, including in litigation, unless they authorize otherwise. On 2026-06-29 the Supreme Court held in Trump v. Slaughter, 6-3, that the FTC's for-cause removal protection is unconstitutional and that Humphrey's Executor no longer controls, while leaving open the Federal Reserve and the tenure of judges on non-Article III courts. Bondi was removed on 2026-04-02 and Todd Blanche has led DOJ in an acting capacity.

timeline.event: AG Bondi issues the memorandum General Policy Regarding Zealous Advocacy on Behalf of the United States to all Department employees: attorneys are to defend presidential policies vigorously, and those who decline to sign briefs, appear, or make good-faith arguments for the administration on personal grounds face discipline and possible termination.

Executive Order 14215, Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies, is signed (Federal Register 2025-02-24). Section 7 provides that the President's and the Attorney General's interpretations of law bind executive branch employees and may not be contradicted in regulations, guidance, or litigation without authorization.

A Georgetown Legal Ethics Journal blog post reports that DOJ immigration litigator Erez Reuveni was fired in April 2025 after acknowledging an error in a court filing in a deportation case, with Bondi saying he had failed to advocate zealously (April 2025; exact day not confirmed, first of month used).
The Supreme Court grants a stay in Trump v. Slaughter, treats the application as a petition for certiorari before judgment, and grants it (Kagan, Sotomayor, Jackson dissenting from the order).
President Trump removes Bondi as Attorney General; Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche leads the department in an acting capacity.

Supreme Court decides Trump v. Slaughter (No. 25-332), 6-3, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts: the FTC's for-cause removal protection violates the separation of powers; Humphrey's Executor is overruled to the extent anything beyond its narrow core remains; the Federal Reserve is left open.
